sources.citation: Perkins, Jeremy, Seunghun J. Lee & Julian Villegas. 2025 [online 2024]. The interaction between tone and duration in Du'an Zhuang. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 54(3): 939-973. doi:10.1017/S0025100324000239 (CC-BY).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Acoustic study of six speakers who 'grew up in a Du'an town': 6 unchecked + 4 checked tones, rhyme duration by syllable type, consonant/vowel inventories after Zhang et al. 1999:101-102, tone descriptions after Zhang et al. 1999, Castro & Hansen 2010 and Li Xulian 2011 (Appendix A). 'stress' appears only in cross-linguistic remarks (Xhosa contour tones on stressed syllables).

sources.citation: Perkins, Jeremy, Seunghun J. Lee & Julian Villegas. 2016. An interplay between F0 and phonation in Du'an Zhuang tone. Proceedings of TAL 2016 (5th International Symposium on Tonal Aspects of Languages), 56-59. doi:10.21437/TAL.2016-12.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. One-speaker production study showing F0 plus creaky phonation distinguish the six unchecked tones of Du'an Zhuang; no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Castro, Andy & Bruce Hansen. 2010. Hongshui He Zhuang dialect intelligibility survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2010-025. Dallas: SIL International. 110 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 5.2 'Tone analysis' and Appendices I/K give tone values for 20 Hongshui He data points (Du'an Gaoling = proposed reference variety for the western/'central' cluster: Du'an, Dahua, Xincheng, N Shanglin); App. E states '(C)V(C)' syllable structure and that 'monosyllabic words dominate in Zhuang'; a full-text search for stress/accent/iamb/unstressed = 0 hits.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.1 'Phonology' (data from Mashan county, Jinchai town, Dongping village): 9 vowels, 23 consonants, 'Zhuang is a tone language, with six stretchy tones and two checked ones', Mashan tone values 53/22/242/24/33/31; no stress statement (a full-text search for stress/accent 0).

sources.note: The only full reference grammar Glottolog lists for cent2009; reviews confirm a 语音 (phonology) chapter, the natural place for a 轻重音/重音 statement. Caveat: the 2015 review classifies Xia'ao as a 桂北土语 variety within Du'an, so its identity vs. zch should be checked against the book's own classification.

sources.note: Review abstracts only: confirm Wei Maofan's 下坳壮语参考语法 covers 语音 (phonology), vocabulary, word classes, syntax; the Zou abstract classifies Xia'ao Zhuang as '广西都安壮语中的桂北土语' (a Guibei-vernacular variety within Du'an county). Nothing on stress in the abstracts; full text needs NCPSSD login.
